back: Ridge built from limestone skeletons of coral polyps in warm, shallow, clear tropical seas.
Above about 18 °C (best roughly 23-29 °C), shallow, clear, salty, unpolluted water; mainly 30° N-30° S, eastern coasts.
Stressed coral (usually by warm water) expels its zooxanthellae and turns white; it starves if stress lasts.
Salt-tolerant tree of sheltered, muddy tropical coasts; prop roots, pneumatophores, salt excretion.
Biodiversity, coastal protection, fisheries and nurseries, tourism, timber and fuel, carbon storage.
Warming and bleaching, acidification, farm run-off, sewage, overfishing, tourism damage, crown-of-thorns starfish, cyclones.
Clearance for shrimp farms, rice and development; cutting for charcoal; pollution; sea-level rise.
Queensland, Australia; more than 2,300 km; World Heritage 1981; 2004 zoning made about a third no-take; Reef 2050.
Fringing (close to shore), barrier (lagoon between reef and shore), atoll (ring round a lagoon).
